title: Hammer: a second hit closes the outline
question: You said the cracks never fully complete, and that multiple hits should surround a chunk so the whole thing falls out as one piece. That was a real gap and not a tuning one: how a given rock splits is a fixed property of the rock, so the one boundary in ten a first blow leaves shut was shut for ever, however many times you hit it. Rock that has already been hit now parts more readily, so a second blow closes what the first left open. Same swing, animated. Does the outline complete now, and are the pieces the size you meant?
context_md: The same cliff face, five blows, 80 frames from the first swing. Counters, because the picture cannot carry them. On the shelf bed (scene=worked, six blows at one spot) the shelf's overload failures went 6 -> 14 and the piece-size ladder gained a 64+ tier and eight more pieces in the 8-15 band. On this cliff face, cells broken 376 -> 406, pieces in flight at once 3 -> 4, largest single piece 8 -> 15 cells. Still short of a gnome-sized block coming out whole on a flat wall: the wound is at ground level and a block there is held from behind, so what completes is the ring nearest the face. If that is the thing still missing, say so and I will go after the size rather than the completion.
